name: Thoth
desc: The Ibis King was one of the Seven Pillars of King Deshret and the Scribe of Scribes. Thoth represented the wisest aspects of King Deshret, inventing the desert script and arcane arts at his king's command.

customize.name: Al-Ahmar
customize.desc: The ruler of the Sumeru desert. He is also known as King Deshret.

customize.text:
Thoth was one of the Seven Sages of King Deshret. Legend has it that King Deshret ruled the desert at the head of several wise retainers, guiding their people to pursue the limits of wisdom. Before the end of his life, Al-Ahmar sealed the Ibis King, the Goat King, and the Crocodile King in the far side of
the final land of dreams for all desert dwellers. Thoth can leave Aaru only when the three people he chooses answer three riddles, left to Al-Ahmar by

customize.name: Nabu Malikata
customize.desc: The Goddess of Flowers, a friend of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and King Deshret.

customize.text:
.
Goudarz
Thoth asked the first riddle to the young noble who sought to save his realm. During his long reign, he betrayed his family and the nobles who supported him, only realizing the error of his ways after his enemies left him nowhere to turn.
Makhaira
Thoth asked the second riddle to the Jinn-blooded dancing girl. She was given as a gift to the tyrant king of Gurabad, and later seized the opportunity to kill him. After getting her vengeance, she reigned as queen for many years until her enemies attempted a coup, and she took her own life.

customize.name: Nefer
customize.desc: The remarkably resourceful owner of the Curatorium of Secrets.

customize.text: Thoth asked the third riddle to Nefer. Although he gave her a special chess set in exchange for her answer, this answer wasn't the one King Deshret was hoping to receive. Nefer knows that the right answer can free the Ibis King, but she doesn't want to let him out. Nefer's cat, Ashru, is one of Thoth's cats that he used to talk to her with.

customize.name: Il Dottore
customize.desc: The Second of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, codenamed The Doctor. Had multiple "segments" of himself, nearly all of which he destroyed in a deal with the Dendro Archon. His real name is Zandik.

customize.text: A few centuries ago, Zandik and a scholar from the

customize.name: Sumeru Akademiya
customize.desc: The Sumeru organization, which exercises administrative control over the region and educates people.

customize.text: fell into the Ibis King's temple. Thoth wanted to ask Zandik the third riddle, but the latter refused because he didn't need Thoth's gift.

customize.name: Layla
customize.desc: A Rtawahist student who specializes in Theoretical Astrology. Heavily prone to somnambulism and locked in a grinding war with sleep deprivation, the problem of restful slumber is a most troubling one to her.

customize.text:
Djer
Two Sumeru dwellers accidentally fell into the Ibis King's temple through the sand. They touched a device King Deshret once used to measure human brain power. That contact caused more knowledge than they could handle to flood into their minds. Thoth replaced that knowledge with simpler, repetitive information. Through the body of a cat, he helped Layla and Djer leave the temple.

customize.name: Reliquary of Truth
customize.desc: An angular box carved from gold and jade. Legend has it that it was once enshrined in a temple deep within Tulaytullah, the Sapphire City.

customize.name: Dialogues of the Desert Sages
customize.desc: A caduceus symbolizing the glory of alchemy, made from special alloys to match its special status. It is exceedingly rigid and heavy, and would probably hurt pretty bad if used as a cudgel.

customize.name: Ibis Piercer
customize.desc: A golden bow forged from the description in the story. If you use it as a normal weapon, you can also view it as a part of a fictional world that has made it off the pages.

customize.name: Ordered Notes
customize.desc: Notes with matching handwriting that have been painstakingly arranged in chronological order. These appear to chronicle a certain person's "adventures" in this place.

imgDesc.text: The Ibis King, the Goat King, and the Crocodile King.
